title: Topological Quantum Algorithms and Braid Compilation

items.title: Certified fixed-dimensional special-unitary input
items.statement: For fixed d in {2,5,8}, define a Cauchy name for an exact target in SU(d) using rational complex matrices with a certified entrywise error; include a separate optional polynomial query-time promise.
proof_obligations: State target domain, matrix norm convention, approximation error, precision encoding, and optional name running time; distinguish exact targets from rational approximants.
Uniqueness compares targets satisfying the coordinate bounds against the same entire approximant sequence Q_b.

items.title: Operator error adds under finite unitary products
items.statement: For finite unitary lists (Ui),(Vi) with ||Ui−Vi||≤εi, the products differ by at most Σ εi.
proof_obligations: Write the telescoping identity and use unitary invariance, submultiplicativity, and the triangle inequality; include the empty product case.

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes

items.axiom_use: None; the finite telescoping estimate is choice-free.

items.title: Operator error bounds measured output variation
items.statement: If U,V are unitaries with ||U−V||≤ε, then any finite POVM has output total-variation distance at most ε on any input density operator.
proof_obligations: Treat pure inputs, decompose a mixed state spectrally, use trace-norm triangle/convexity, and apply the measurement-variation theorem.

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes
John Preskill, Quantum Computation, Chapter 2: Foundations I: States and Ensembles

items.axiom_use: None; finite-dimensional spectral decomposition and trace-norm inequalities are choice-free.

items.title: Finite anyon task and promise interface
items.statement: A finite decision/search promise on encoded fusion-tree inputs, with braid-word and projective-measurement access and an explicit acceptance/output rule.
proof_obligations: Define finite input/output alphabets, promise domain, braid and fusion-measurement access, and correctness only on promised instances.

items.title: Fusion-tree task input encoding
items.statement: A finite admissible fusion tree, its simple-charge edge labels, total charge, multiplicity indices, and a fixed computational basis encoding, with validity determined at every vertex by the fusion rules. An isometry is named through a declared background codebook; an isometry varying as classical input needs an exact finite description language, with no universal finite encoding of arbitrary complex isometries.
proof_obligations: Define encoded labels and local admissibility; include empty/single-leaf boundary conventions or exclude them explicitly; distinguish an encoding from a physical preparation.

items.axiom_use: None; finite labels and fixed trees are used.

items.title: Anyon compiler resource ledger
items.statement: Record braid length, fusion-measurement count, precision bits, classical search time, logical operator error, leakage amplitude/probability, and phase correction cost as separate coordinates. Also retain the complete applicable QC circuit cost record (including description, gates, depth, wires, ancillas and named oracle queries) and a separate total nonoracle gate count.
proof_obligations: Specify which operations and encodings each coordinate counts; preserve inapplicable versus zero; state no hidden free braid, measurement, oracle, or phase correction.

items.title: Fusion-channel measurement access
items.statement: For an adjacent pair in a fusion tree, define the projectors onto its allowed total-charge channels and the corresponding finite projective measurement, including post-measurement unnormalized vectors.
proof_obligations: Specify mutually orthogonal channel subspaces, zero-probability outcomes, and the chosen fusion-tree basis convention.

items.title: Arbitrary-n triple-anyon fixed-charge code
items.statement: For n≥1 and c∈{1,τ} with V(τ^n→c)≠0, group the 3n ordered τ charges into n consecutive triples, require each triple total to be τ, and then fuse the n triple outputs to c. The grouped-tree coordinates identify this code with (C²)^{⊗n}⊗V(τ^n→c); associator maps transport it to the declared fixed tree and define an isometry J_{n,c} and projector P_{n,c}=J_{n,c}J_{n,c}^*.
proof_obligations: Compute the three-anyon total-τ multiplicity from the Fibonacci fusion recurrence, construct the grouped orthonormal basis including all spectator paths, and verify reassociation preserves the isometry and projector.

references.title: John Preskill, Lecture Notes for Physics 219: Quantum Computation, Chapter 9: Topological Quantum Computation

items.axiom_use: None; the grouped fusion-tree basis, finite tensor products, and unitary reassociation are choice-free.

items.title: Braid phase reference and correction ledger
items.statement: For a braid word b of exponent sum k, record normalized lift z^kB(b), physical phase λ^k with λ=R1 z^{-1}, and the cost/interface for correcting that phase under coherent control.
proof_obligations: Define exponent sum, scalar character, standalone versus controlled use, and charge-independent phase tracking; do not silently discard a controlled phase.

items.axiom_use: None; this is finite word bookkeeping and unit-modulus scalar algebra.

items.title: A triple braid acts identically on fusion spectators
items.statement: In the grouped fusion-tree decomposition of V(τ^{3n}→c) into local triple spaces V(τ^3→a_i) and the outer spectator space V(a_1⊗⋯⊗a_n→c), a braid word supported in the i-th triple acts as its fixed-total-charge matrix on V(τ^3→a_i) tensored with the identity on every other triple and spectator factor. The rebracketing to the fixed left-associated tree is unitary, so the statement holds there as well.
proof_obligations: Write the grouped orthonormal basis as local triple paths and an outer fusion path; apply the braid action definition to one local morphism factor and prove the tensor/direct-sum norm facts used by consumers.

items.title: Fusion measurement branches are normalized exactly when nonzero
items.statement: For every normalized input, channel probabilities sum to one; a conditional branch vector exists precisely when its projector has nonzero probability, and is the normalized projection.
proof_obligations: Prove orthogonal resolution of identity, Born probabilities, branch norm, normalization, and the zero branch boundary.

items.title: Exhaustive certified Fibonacci B6 block-pair search
items.statement: Dovetail all normalized six-strand braid words and precision requests; certify both SU(5) and SU(8) block Frobenius errors below rational ε; return a common word, certificates, length, exponent sum, and phase ledger when found.
proof_obligations: Specify finite word enumeration, Cauchy approximation and rational strict-error certificate; make no word-length or runtime bound; do not claim termination in the definition.

items.title: Finite adiabatic braid compilation input
items.statement: Specify a finite C² uniformly gapped path, constant-rank band, preparation isometry, schedule, measurement, a separate in-band transport error εtr identifying the band action with the selected Fibonacci braid, and phase record. Explicit unitary fusion-space coordinates Q0,Q1 define the logical target and both band identifications; categorical action does not assert physical realization.
proof_obligations: State all path hypotheses, exact model assumptions, preparation and measurement inputs, and explicitly separate in-band identification from JRS leakage.

items.title: Standalone and controlled phase accounting for a fixed-sector braid
items.statement: The physical Fibonacci braid word differs from its normalized lift by λ^k on every fixed-charge block; this scalar leaves standalone probabilities invariant but becomes relative under coherent control.
proof_obligations: Prove the word scalar by exponent additivity, apply standalone phase invariance, and show a controlled branch acquires a relative phase.

items.title: Certified B6 block-pair search terminates
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. For every certified Cauchy input pair
$(T_5,T_8)\in SU(5)\times SU(8)$ and every positive rational
$\varepsilon$, the exhaustive compiler of
[[alg-qa-37-exhaustive-b6-block-pair-compiler]] halts with one six-strand
Fibonacci braid word whose normalized total-charge-$1$ and total-charge-$\tau$
matrices are each within operator norm $\varepsilon$ of $T_5,T_8$,
respectively. Density proves termination, but this result gives no useful
joint-block word-length or search-time bound.
proof_obligations: Use joint density to choose one word with a strict Frobenius margin in both blocks; Cauchy certificates eventually verify it; dovetailing reaches that word and precision.

items.title: Finite JRS leakage amplitude and probability
items.statement: For the specified band and schedule, leakage amplitude is at most A_m(1) and leakage probability at most A_m(1)^2, with A_m exactly the JRS expression; the theorem makes no in-band braid-holonomy claim.
proof_obligations: Substitute the finite model into the JRS theorem and derive probability by squaring the amplitude bound; state the no-transport inference.

references.title: Sabine Jansen, Mary-Beth Ruskai, and Ruedi Seiler, Bounds for the adiabatic approximation with applications to quantum computation
Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms

items.title: The generated normalized Fibonacci lifts are dense in SU(2)
items.statement: Under ACω and the fixed Fibonacci convention, the closure of the subgroup generated by zB1,zB2, with z=exp(3πi/10), is SU(2).
proof_obligations: Verify det(zBj)=1; identify the projective subgroup and its full preimage as Λ∪(-Λ); use density of the full preimage and connectedness to prove Λ itself is dense; state ACω uses.

items.title: Finite braid compilation and adiabatic error budget
items.statement: If compiled logical circuit error is εc, independently supplied in-band transport error is εtr, JRS leakage amplitude is A_m(1), and measurement implementation variation is εm, then total output variation is at most εc+εtr+A_m(1)+εm.
proof_obligations: Compare compiled and ideal band outputs, add in-band mismatch and leakage in vector/operator norm, convert to trace distance and measurement variation, then add εm; do not infer εtr from JRS.

items.title: One B6 braid approximates an encoded two-qubit gate
items.statement: Assume ACω. For U∈U(4), choose determinant-corrected SU(5) and SU(8) extensions; one normalized B6 word approximates both, giving logical error and leakage at most ε in both fixed-charge blocks, with its common physical phase explicitly recorded.
proof_obligations: Verify the target extensions are special unitary; apply termination; restrict ambient norm error to code and complement; account for one common phase under coherent control.

items.statement: Let z=exp(3πi/10), define normalized generators zB1,zB2 and include their inverses as a finite alphabet; specify exact labels, matrices, chirality and inverse convention.
proof_obligations: Verify determinant one and unitarity from the local matrix supplier; define inverse-closed alphabet and dense closure; state that this does not supply a concrete base-net table.

items.statement: A mathematical braid compiler result is physically instantiated only with a separate record for state preparation, Hamiltonian path, gap, schedule, band-to-F/R identification, phase reference, locality and hardware error terms; none is supplied by density or SK alone.
proof_obligations: Define the required physical evidence as independent inputs; state that algebraic compilation and JRS leakage do not establish material realization or locality.

items.statement: Invoke the published SU(2) SK recursion on the fixed inverse-closed dense Fibonacci alphabet, a fixed certified finite base-net certificate, exact target Cauchy input, and rational tolerance.
proof_obligations: List exact inputs and outputs; define the fixed base-net certificate as supplied data; distinguish exact-real and finite-precision interfaces and include phase exponent output.

items.title: Fibonacci SU(2) compiler error, length, and bit cost
items.statement: With the fixed base-net certificate and exact published hypotheses, the compiler returns W with ||S-W||≤ε, length at most L0 5^J=O(log^3.97(1/ε)); polynomial-time Cauchy names meet the published bit bound O((N+sε)^(c+10)).
proof_obligations: Instantiate the error recurrence and length bound; state J as the least level; separately state polynomial-name bit-cost assumptions; preserve the algebraic-entry and base-net hypotheses.

items.title: Arbitrary-size triple-encoded projective braid approximation
items.statement: Assume ACω. Every finite n-qubit unitary and fixed total charge admits a finite Fibonacci braid word with uniform spectator-safe projective logical error and leakage at most ε; the proof composes exact QSD, SK-compiled one-qubit gates, and joint-density two-qubit extensions, with summed error. It gives no useful joint-block word-length/time bound.
proof_obligations: Handle n=1 and empty/trivial decompositions; obtain a finite QSD list; compile each one-qubit SU(2) representative and each two-qubit gate at tolerance ε/M; extend to spectators; telescope; track aggregate phases; avoid the earlier arbitrary-n conclusion as a premise.

title: Topological Quantum Algorithms and Braid Compilation — Examples

items.title: Fibonacci fusion measurement branches and zero outcomes
items.statement: For a normalized vector a|1>+b|τ> in a two-channel fusion space, probabilities are |a|² and |b|²; normalize only a nonzero projected branch, and treat a zero coefficient as a zero-probability branch with no conditional state.
proof_obligations: Compute channel projectors, probabilities, normalized branch states, both zero boundary cases, and explain the TikZ measurement circuit convention.

items.title: A discarded global phase changes a controlled computation
items.statement: I and −I have identical standalone action on rays, but controlled-I and controlled-(−I) differ: on |+> they produce |+> and |−>, respectively.
proof_obligations: Compute controlled block matrices and X-basis probabilities; identify standalone projective equality and the relative control phase; include a TikZ circuit.

items.statement: For U=I4, determinant-corrected targets are I5 and I8; the empty braid certifies exact zero block error, zero leakage and exponent sum zero.
proof_obligations: Evaluate determinants and empty-word action in both blocks; confirm boundary error and physical phase.

items.title: Fibonacci SK level and symbolic gate budget
items.statement: For η0=2^-13 and ε=2^-14, the SK recurrence has first admissible level J=2 and length at most 25L0; for M QSD factors, allocate per-factor tolerance min(ε/(2M),η0/2), while keeping base-net size, B6 search work, measurement and phase costs explicit. Actual factor approximations use the arbitrary-n encoding theorem under ACω on an admissible nonzero-spectator code, and errors are relative to the recorded product phase.
proof_obligations: Calculate η1 and η2 exactly as powers of two; verify minimality of J and sum the per-gate error allocation; flag L0 as a supplied certified net input.
